annotations.text:
A version of Lilo I think is better.

Seven screens replace fourteen. The trip is one page — countdown on the cover, who's in with real state, whatever is waiting on the group, the plan as days. No tabs. Add anything is one field that takes a pasted confirmation, a link or a sentence and proposes what it read; the parse preview is the point, since ParsedBooking already carries every field shown there.

Who's in is the screen Lilo does not have: a grid answering flights, room and bag for each person at once. Saved is where Eat and Experience content lives once the tabs go — one list, filtered, with anything unresolved floating to the top. A second trip sits at the end to show the system holding under a different photo and a different accent.

The arguments behind all of it are on the board below. Sample content throughout — names, times, prices and references are invented.

Same layout, different trip.

The accent is derived from the cover: Amalfi's terracotta gives #98673E, Tokyo's neon-and-dusk gives #188295. Both are darkened until they clear 4.5:1 on white, so the colour that identifies a trip is also the colour that is safe to set type in.

That is what retires the cyan contrast problem rather than patching it — cyan goes back to being the app mark and never has to carry text again.
The case, in three parts. If you disagree with an argument, the screens it produced are wrong — start here rather than with the pixels.
